shared_elements: predatory animal (feline-like) with large head shown with forelimbs/paws
vertical stacking of figures in registers/tiers
justification: Both surfaces combine a broad-headed predatory animal with clawed forelimbs and a human head/figure, stacked in a vertical tier with a crosshatched net-like patterned zone, and both render bodies as blocky, schematic, frontally splayed forms with oversized heads. The clearest difference is that A is a multi-register composition with a wide cast (birds, several quadrupeds, snake-like and small human figures) arranged in narrative rows, while B shows only a compact two- or three-figure stacked group, so the specific accompanying motifs and their sequence do not correspond.
